title: Non-blocking follow-up from backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider-followups's PR #370 review
description: Non-blocking finding from pr-reviewer's PR #370 review of backend-ibkr-primary-data-provider-followups (accepted). PR #370's `_resolve_stk_conid` duplicate-description fix (first non-null `description` wins for a repeated conid, rather than the last row in payload order silently overwriting it) is itself verified correct -- manually confirmed with a two-distinct-conid scenario (conid A with duplicate rows `["NASDAQ", None]`, conid B single row `"NYSE"`): the fixed code correctly returns `None` (both now count as primary-exchange candidates, genuinely ambiguous) where the pre-fix last-wins logic incorrectly returned conid B's conid (A's retained description got clobbered to `None` by the second row, making B look like the only primary candidate). However, the two new tests PR #370 actually shipped for this fix (`test_duplicate_rows_for_the_same_conid_keep_the_first_non_null_description`, `test_duplicate_rows_for_the_same_conid_disagreeing_on_description_keep_the_first`) only ever construct a single distinct conid (265598) with duplicate rows for it -- in that shape, `_resolve_stk_conid`'s `len(candidates) == 1` branch returns the sole conid unconditionally, before the retained `description` value is ever consulted. Verified directly: reverting the fix back to the old unconditional-overwrite (`candidates[conid] = description if isinstance(description, str) else None`) still makes both of these tests pass unchanged. So neither test actually exercises or guards the distinguishing behavior the fix introduces -- a future regression back to last-wins semantics would ship silently with these two tests still green.

checklist.step: Add a test to tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py's TestResolveConid class with two distinct conids, where one has duplicate rows disagreeing on description (e.g. first row description naming a primary US exchange, a later row null or a different non-primary value) and the other is a single-row primary-exchange candidate -- asserting resolve_conid/_resolve_stk_conid returns None (genuinely ambiguous, both count as primary) rather than silently picking the other candidate. Confirm this new test fails against the pre-fix (last-wins) logic and passes against the current code, the same way this finding's own review did manually.

decisions.decision: Added `test_duplicate_description_retention_is_exercised_against_a_second_distinct_conid` to `TestResolveConid` using the exact two-distinct-conid payload shape the task description itself verified during review (conid 111 with duplicate rows `["NASDAQ", None]`, conid 222 with a single `"NYSE"` row), asserting `resolve_conid` returns `None`. Did not also add a disagreeing-non-null-description variant at this two-conid shape (e.g. `["NASDAQ", "SOME_OTHER_VENUE"]` for conid 111) as a second new test -- the single new test already exercises the exact gap the finding identified (the `len(candidates) == 1` shortcut no longer short-circuits before the retention logic runs), and a second nearly-identical two-conid case would be redundant coverage rather than closing a distinct gap; the existing single-conid disagreeing-description test already covers that the first-non-null-wins rule picks the right winner when it's not null vs. null.
decisions.rationale: Mutation-tested directly per this task's own instructions: temporarily reverted `_resolve_stk_conid` to the old unconditional last-wins assignment (`candidates[conid] = description if isinstance(description, str) else None`, dropping the `if conid not in candidates or candidates[conid] is None` guard) and reran `TestResolveConid` -- the new test failed (`resolve_conid('BAR') == 222`, not `None`) while all other existing tests in the class still passed unchanged, confirming the new test is the one that actually catches a regression to last-wins semantics that the two originally-shipped tests (both single-conid) do not. Restored the fix immediately after and reran the full class to confirm all 25 tests (now including the new one) pass against the current code.
